To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the recent rapid increase in global methane concentrations, which are now approaching the highest levels in the past two millennia, is predominantly biogenic, most likely from agriculture, with smaller contributions from fossil fuels and wetlands.
(a) the recent rise in atmospheric methane concentrations is predominantly anthropogenic and (b) methane emissions are increasing faster than previously thought, primarily from agriculture.

(1) methane emissions from agriculture are the largest source of anthropogenic methane emissions; (2) the recent rapid growth in methane concentrations in the atmosphere is predominantly biogenic and most likely from agricultural sources; (3) methane emissions from fossil fuel use are smaller and less uncertain; (4) the growth in methane concentrations is not due to a reduction in atmospheric methane sinks; and (5) the growth in atmospheric methane is not due to an increase in emissions from wetlands.
